headline: Sustainability is using resources at a rate they can regenerate—taking only what replenishes
universal_truth: You can't draw from a well forever if you take more than it refills; match consumption to regeneration
fun_facts: Earth Overshoot Day—when humanity has used a year's worth of resources—falls earlier each year
Sustainable fishing quotas allow fish populations to recover; overfishing has collapsed many fisheries
Bamboo is considered sustainable because it grows up to 35 inches per day
discussion_questions: What resources are you consuming faster than they regenerate?
Where do you need to reduce consumption or increase regeneration?
What sustainable practices have you adopted?

hook.script: Imagine a bank account where you spend more than you earn. Eventually, you're broke. Now imagine that with forests, fisheries, energy, even your own health. Sustainability is matching withdrawal to deposit—taking only what replenishes.

cliff.script: Unsustainable practices seem fine—until they're not. The crash comes when resources are exhausted. How do we live sustainably?

options.text: Sustainable living requires tracking resources, consuming at or below regeneration rates, and actively investing in renewal—not just taking less, but ensuring replenishment
options.response: Yes. Sustainability needs both sides: reduce consumption AND support regeneration. It's not just taking less—it's ensuring what you take can be replaced.
Using less helps, but true sustainability also requires regeneration...

fact1.title: Regeneration Rates
fact1.script: Every resource has a regeneration rate. Forests regrow at certain speeds. Energy can be renewed. Even personal energy replenishes. Sustainability means matching consumption to regeneration.

fact2.title: Delayed Consequences
fact2.script: Unsustainable practices don't fail immediately—consequences lag. This makes it easy to ignore them. By the time problems are obvious, damage is done. Sustainability requires thinking ahead.

fact3.title: Personal Sustainability
fact3.script: Your energy, health, and relationships are resources too. Burnout is unsustainability—consuming faster than regenerating. Recovery time matters. Sustainable living applies to you, not just the planet.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: You can't draw from a well forever if you take more than it refills. Match consumption to regeneration—in resources and in life.

outro.script: That's Day 236. Tomorrow, we'll explore weather patterns over time—climate. Until then, audit one resource for sustainability.

growTrack.title: Sustainability Check - Consumption vs Regeneration
growTrack.activity: Pick a resource you depend on: energy, time, money, relationships, health. Are you consuming faster than it regenerates? What would sustainable look like? Sometimes small reductions in consumption, combined with investment in regeneration, transform unsustainable patterns.
